final3.name: Nordic Techo Planner + Refills
final3.case_for: Only idea with a genuine repeat mechanic (annual refill) and a launch window (Aug 2027 school-year edition) that gives 9 months to validate before cash is committed. Pure design/pricing/brand work plays to the founders. Demand is proven in the category (Hobonichi >1M copies, Papier >GBP 40M) even if not proven for an unknown Nordic brand. Cheapest to test: a waitlist/preorder costs EUR 300-500. Red team is right that defensibility is ~1-2 and that 3.1x is razor-thin on an unverified landed cost; I keep it first only because the downside is fully testable before spend.
final3.key_risks: Layout is a file: Burde, Etsy/POD sellers, Hobonichi's Nordic reseller can copy within a season. Single-source Tomoe-type paper (Wonderland 222 had to drop Sanzen for 2026, source wellappointeddesk/wonderland222 URLs from red team); MOQ and price unknown. Margin 3.1x only at EUR 9 landed; at EUR 11 it is 2.5x and fails. Paid CAC EUR 15-25 > contribution EUR 11-13; wholesale ~36% margin fails target. Dated stock is near worthless after January. All Nordic demand numbers are ASSUMPTION; confidence Low.
final3.must_fix_before_sourcing: (1) Written paper+print quote with MOQ, lead time and landed <= EUR 7-8 incl. freight; if the Tomoe-type paper is unobtainable, drop. (2) 150-300 PAID preorders (not waitlist signups) at ~EUR 35 for an Aug-2027 edition. (3) Show an organic channel (TikTok/IG audience) delivering sign-ups at near-zero CAC. (4) A defensible hook: exclusive artist/designer licence or proprietary cover/refill format. (5) Decide DTC-only; no Amazon/wholesale.

final3.name: Nordic Bird-Safe Window Kit / Decal Sets
final3.case_for: Best regulatory/capital profile (no CE, no tooling, flat letterbox-able kit, ~EUR 4-5k first order, ~79% product margin) and the only one where the ex-VELUX glazing credibility is a real, usable asset: glazing installers, BRF/co-op boards and architects are a B2B/SEO channel that escapes the EUR 6-13 consumer anchor. The product has a genuine technical argument (dense 10 cm-or-finer grid with install template) that cheap silhouette stickers do not meet.
final3.key_risks: Defensibility ~1: printed dots are trivial to copy; Solarscreen already makes 9 mm/90 mm dot film and Etsy/eBay/Kaufland sell dot sets. The efficacy claim is both the differentiator and a UCPD liability; independent test may cost > EUR 2k (ASSUMPTION) and certifies a pattern others can replicate. One-off purchase, near-zero repeat. Paid CAC (EUR 35-45) far exceeds contribution (EUR 8-10). Adhesion outdoors in Nordic winter, low-E glass incompatibility (Lee Valley warning per red team). Year-1 orders may be 100-300, not 600-1,000. Revenue ceiling ~EUR 12-19k ex-VAT per 1,000 kits.
final3.must_fix_before_sourcing: (1) Measured demand: Google Trends/keyword volume in sv/da/de plus EUR 300 preorder test, gate ~150 paid preorders. (2) Signed partnership or endorsement from a bird NGO (BirdLife Sverige / DOF) or an independent efficacy test; without it, do not use any 'bird-safe' wording. (3) Three supplier quotes confirming landed <= EUR 4 and an outdoor adhesive rated for Nordic temperatures. (4) Validate one B2B route (BRF boards or glazing installers, ex-VELUX network) as primary channel. (5) Verify SE/DK EPR thresholds and GPSR costs.

final3.name: Trickle-vent refresh kit
final3.case_for: Smallest capital at risk (~EUR 1.8k first order, ~500 kits), no tooling beyond a die cutter, real physical problem (condensation, dust, pollen), and the strongest direct use of founders' building-industry knowledge: a fit-to-profile compatibility library and installer/window-maker relationships are the only moat in this field that is slow to copy and is not a mere file. A B2B repositioning (installers, housing associations, window makers, multipacks) is credible via ex-VELUX contacts. It is third because the loss is capped, not because the upside is large.
final3.key_risks: Demand is entirely ASSUMPTION and no visible replacement-filter category appeared in red-team searches. Kit at EUR 19-25 is about the price of a whole new Schellenberg vent (EUR 23.99 OBI; Universal EUR 13.95 Hornbach, snippet only), capping price and repeat. Contribution about zero after fees, postage, wrong-fit returns and CAC. OEMs (Volution/FRESH via Onninen, VILPE) can sell their own refills. Compatibility library multiplies SKUs against 10 h/week. Winter-season sales window. Trend score 1: tiny niche. Must avoid mould/health/biocide claims.
final3.must_fix_before_sourcing: (1) Cheap demand test: SEO how-to page plus EUR 200 ads in SE/DK/DE; gate email cost < EUR 5 and > 3% preorder intent. (2) Interview 5-10 installers/housing-association maintenance leads via ex-VELUX network and get one pilot order or LOI at EUR 3-6/unit multipack. (3) Map the 3-5 most common vent profiles in SE/DK and prove a universal-fit design (one or two SKUs, not a library). (4) Price check against replacement vents; kill if consumer price cannot sit well under EUR 15 or B2B does not materialise.

reserve.name: Nordic punch-needle bag-charm kits
reserve.reason: Only candidate with a visible (if fad-driven and US-centric) trend and a design-led edge, but Clas Ohlson, Panduro, Kit Company, DMC, Crafter's Companion and Etsy already own the shelf at EUR 9-17 versus the EUR 26 target, and defensibility is ~1. Activate only if a EUR 1k presale (finished-charm positioning at EUR 29-35, exclusive Nordic artist/architect licence, CVR > 2%, organic CAC < EUR 8) clearly passes.

cuts.name: Refillable silvervine cat toy
cuts.reason: Refillable silvervine plush already sold by Jackson Galaxy, Spot, Gigwi, SmartyKat and KONG (stocked at Apotea.se) at about half the price; no moat, EUR 2.5-7 loose silvervine undercuts the refill, and a EUR 20-35 CAC against ~EUR 8 contribution is structurally loss-making.

cuts.name: Radiator glove and boot dryer shelf
cuts.reason: Commodity bent-steel accessory vs EUR 8-20 radiator airers and ADAX electric shelves, one purchase per customer, seasonal Oct-Feb, hot-surface liability, wholesale/Amazon break the margin target, and demand for a glove-specific category is unevidenced.

honest_overall_assessment: This is the best of a weak field, not a set of genuinely good ideas. Every red-team pass, and my own reading of the evidence, converges on the same fatal flaw: near-zero defensibility, which the brief weights highest. In all six, a copy needs only a file, a die cutter or a Chinese sewing/printing factory, and most face verified incumbents already on the Nordic shelf (Burde, Hobonichi via Paper Whisper, Clas Ohlson, KONG at Apotea, Solarscreen). Worse, in five of six paid acquisition (CAC EUR 15-45) exceeds first-order contribution (EUR 8-13), so growth depends on organic TikTok/IG luck that 10 founder-hours/week cannot reliably produce. Every market size, landed cost, conversion and CAC figure is ASSUMPTION or vendor-blog benchmark; confidence is Low across the board and no supplier quote exists for any idea. The 65%/3x margin claims are product-level and hold only on unverified landed costs, then fail at wholesale or Amazon. I did not rerun searches: the red teams' evidence was consistent across both reviewers and the analysts' own concessions, and fresh search would not change the structural conclusion. Realistic expectation for the top 3: year-1 revenue of EUR 5-25k and roughly break-even at best. The sensible use of EUR 5-10k is NOT a production order: spend EUR 300-500 per idea on preorder/waitlist tests (about EUR 1-1.5k total), commit to a first order only if one passes its paid-preorder gate, and otherwise treat the null result as the finding and widen the search toward products with a proprietary mechanism, a consumable, or a B2B channel where the founders' ex-VELUX/Nilfisk networks are an actual structural advantage.
